newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-WILLIAMS BEATS MAJOLI IN CALIFORNIA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WILLIAMS BEATS MAJOLI IN CALIFORNIA.

text.p: American
teenager Venus Williams beat her first top-10 player,
upsetting fifth-seed Iva Majoli of Croatia 7-5 3-6 7-5 in the
$1.25 million Evert Cup women's tennis tournament on Tuesday
The 16-year-old Williams, playing in her first tournament
of the year, qualified for the tournament on a wild card.
Williams, ranked 211th, won two qualifying rounds and
three main draw matches to reach the quarterfinals where she
will play American Lindsay Davenport.
The fourth-seeded Davenport moved into the quarterfinals
with a quick 6-2 6-1 third round victory over 14th-seeded
Ruxandra Dragomir of Romania.
Willims and Majoli went toe-to-toe under a scorching sun
for two hours and 33 minutes.
The real drama came in the 10th game of the third set with
Williams serving. She faced two match points on her serve in
that game, but saved them both, the second with a 109 mph (175
kph) ace.
Majoli looked very fatigued in the 11th game, posting four
straight unforced errors to lose her serve at love.
Serving in the last game, Williams finally took advantage
of her third match point with an incredible service winner.
"Yes, I feel good beating a top 10 player," Williams said.
"I don't think about playing top 10 players (or) that I got
all these points, look at all this prestige. I try to go out
there and stay relaxed.
"Even in this match today, I wasn't playing anywhere near
what I can play," Williams said. "I wasn't attacking the short
balls. The high balls, I wasn't taking those out of the air.
And, on the return of serves, I wasn't attacking those. It
was nothing near what I can do, and I know that if I can go
out there and just go for broke, you guys will see a real
match."
